READ_THIS_FIRST.what_this_is: A PROPOSAL, so that the owner ratifies or corrects rather than designs from scratch. Every row below carries the repo evidence that supports it, with file and line. Rows with no evidence, or with conflicting evidence, are marked CONTESTED and are LEFT EMPTY. They are not filled in by position.
what_this_is_NOT: Not a ratification. required_run_bindings[6] tks_to_cas_crosswalk_sha256 stays EMPTY until the owner signs something.

Not a tested crosswalk. The registry's required_resolution says 'publish and TEST a bijective code-and-meaning crosswalk'. Nothing here is tested. Ratifying this proposal publishes it; it does not test it.

Not bijective on all three axes. The Noetic axis is proposed complete (10/10 evidenced). The symbol-index axis is proposed complete as a code map (40/40 rows) but meaning-clean on only 35/40 (3 WEAK, 2 DIVERGENT). The WORLD axis is 4 of 4 rows CONTESTED and is the reason this artifact cannot be hashed into binding 6 as it stands.
Not a licence to capture. GATE2_ITEM4_PREREGISTRATION.md:32 requires B5 committed and hashed BEFORE capture, and 9.2 condition 3 requires the ratification to be DATED before the capture timestamp.
READ_THIS_FIRST.honest_headline: Two of the three axes are evidenced well enough to ratify on sight. The third - what TKS World A/B/C/D maps onto in CAS - has two mutually exclusive answers, both live in the repo, and the owner has to make that call. Those are the four rows that need a decision.

known_conflict_1_verbatim.finding: TKS v7.4 and owner-locked original fixtures use A1-D10, while normalized canon_elements_40.json uses A0-D9. This is a cyclic index remapping, not a harmless display change.
known_conflict_1_verbatim.required_resolution: Publish and test a bijective code-and-meaning crosswalk; store both source_symbol and normalized_index in every artifact.

known_conflict_world_axis_verbatim.finding: Existing artifacts map the four native TKS Worlds both to CAS Domains P/C/E/O and to CAS Registers T/A/f/E, although Domain and Register are separate CAS axes. A single World label therefore cannot be silently treated as both.
known_conflict_world_axis_verbatim.required_resolution: Preserve native TKS World as its own field, define separate versioned World-to-Domain and World-to-Register hypotheses, and test each crosswalk as a distinct multi-head probe rather than declaring an identity.

registry.future_agent_rule_2_verbatim: Do not remap A1-D10 to A0-D9 by position without a tested crosswalk.
registry.compliance_statement: No row in this proposal was derived by position. The Noetic axis rows are derived from NAME identity in an owner source. The symbol-index rows are derived from NAME semantics read from both files. The World rows are not derived at all - they are presented as two competing hypotheses with their evidence, and left for the owner.

pre_registration.status: LOCKED - this proposal conforms to it and does not modify it
pre_registration.B5_row_verbatim: Owner ratification of the TKS<->CAS crosswalk used by Arm D (Domain A/B/C/D <-> CAS Domain, TKS Noetic 1..10 <-> CAS ^1..^9,^0) - required for required_run_bindings[6] tks_to_cas_crosswalk_sha256, currently empty
pre_registration.line_32_verbatim: B5 must be committed and hashed BEFORE capture, not after. If the crosswalk is ratified only after the numbers exist, the owner - who holds the prior under test - controls whether an Arm A loss to Arm D 'counts'. That is unfalsifiability by procedure and this document forbids it.
pre_registration.note_on_the_B5_wording: The B5 row names 'Domain A/B/C/D <-> CAS Domain'. Measured this session, that phrasing prejudges the contested axis: it assumes the World maps to CAS Domain. The pre-registration itself contradicts that at section 2.4, which flags tks_world_to_cas_domain_and_register_collision as unresolved, and the Gate 2 item 4 holdout bank asserts Register and carries no CAS-domain field at all. This proposal therefore treats the second factor as OPEN rather than as Domain-by-assumption. That is a widening of B5's question, not a change to any frozen threshold, criterion, control, or unit of analysis - nothing in sections 5-9 is touched.

correction_to_the_task_brief.claim_checked: The build brief said the stage9 40E fixture metadata 'carries legacy_domain / legacy_element_code / element_domain / element_noetic_tks fields'.
correction_to_the_task_brief.measured: Those fields are split across TWO DIFFERENT artifacts, and conflating them would have produced a wrong crosswalk. The Gate 2 item 4 holdout bank (git blob 165df0f6, branch experiment/cas-probe-pythia) has exactly 28 keys and NONE of them is legacy_domain or legacy_element_code; it carries element_domain / element_domain_name / element_register / element_register_name / element_noetic_tks / element_cas_noetic / element_noetic_name, and its 'element_domain' field holds the TKS WORLD LETTER, not a CAS domain. The legacy_domain / legacy_element_code fields live in a DIFFERENT artifact - the 20260527 scenarios export in D:/tksCAS-archive - and in noetic-compass-scaffold/noetic-compass/cas-native/belief/tks40_specificity.py:71-72. Those two artifacts assert OPPOSITE second factors. Treating them as one de-facto crosswalk is exactly the error this artifact exists to prevent.
correction_to_the_task_brief.consequence_for_this_proposal: The 'existing de-facto crosswalk' is not one crosswalk. It is two, they disagree on the World axis, and they agree on the Noetic axis. That split is precisely the EVIDENCED / CONTESTED boundary drawn below.

axis_1_tks_noetic_position_to_cas_noetic.strength_summary: This is the strong half. It is evidenced by an OWNER source (the owner's own element titles put the CAS Noetic name at each TKS position, in all four worlds - 40 corroborations for 10 rows), by repository-normative CAS authority (Clarification 1 names), by two live code modules, and by two independently-built 8,320-row fixtures that agree with each other on this axis even though they disagree on the World axis. Eight of ten owner title words are byte-identical to the Clarification 1 names; the two that are not ('Above' vs 'Above/Cause', 'Below' vs 'Below/Effect') are prefixes of them.
axis_1_tks_noetic_position_to_cas_noetic.the_one_assistant_judgement_in_this_axis: That the owner's 'Above'/'Below' mean the canonical 'Above/Cause'/'Below/Effect' rather than a spatial above/below. Supporting: the owner's A8/A9 sit in the same positions the canon names 'Divine Cause'/'Spiritual Effect' and the bank names 'Above/Cause'/'Below/Effect'. Against: the zero-based canon reads exactly these two positions SPATIALLY in the Physical world (D8 'Physical Elevation', D9 'Physical Foundation'). Flagged here rather than buried; see axis 3 rows D8/D9.

counter_evidence.detail: Positions 1..9 map to the same digit. Position 10 maps to ^0. Everything that could go wrong in this axis is concentrated here, so it is worth stating what supports it independently of the digit pattern: the owner's own titles A10/B10/C10/D10 are 'Spiritual Idea' / 'Mental Idea' / 'Emotional Idea' / 'Physical Idea', and Clarification 1 names ^0 'Idea'. The zero-based TKS canon independently puts Idea at position 0 (B0 'a specific idea/concept', C0 'the idea of an emotion', D0 'Concept of a physical thing'). Three sources, two of them non-positional.

evidence_against.what_it_says: TKS encoded both cross-products with the same 4-Worlds axis. Reframed in secular universal terms as 4 Registers (T, A, f, E), this axis applies consistently across all CAS primitives - both Noetic-level (10 x 4 = 40 Cognitive-State-by-Register combinations) and Drive-level (7 x 4 = 28 Drive-by-Register combinations).
evidence_against.why_it_bites: The highest-precedence artifact in this dispute says the 40-Element cross-product's second factor is REGISTER, not Domain. If that is right, H-WD is wrong.

evidence_for.what_it_says: '10 Noetics x 4 Worlds = 40 Elements' ... 'Reframed in secular universal terms as 4 Registers (T, A, f, E), this axis applies consistently across all CAS primitives' ... 'CAS v7.4 lost the Worlds axis in translation from TKS. CAS v7.5 restores it on secular universal basis as the Phenomenological Register.'
evidence_for.note: This is the HIGHEST-PRECEDENCE artifact asserting either hypothesis. But its registry precedence line is scoped: 'Operational CAS authority for Noetic NAMES AND DEFINITIONS' (registry line 47). It is not declared authority for the World axis. So even the strongest evidence here is out of its own stated scope.

evidence_for.what_it_says: |T Transcendent = 1st World (highest/most abstract); |A Analytical = 2nd World; |f Affective = 3rd World; |E Embodied = 4th World (lowest/most concrete).
evidence_for.note: IMPORTANT: this table maps by WORLD ORDINAL POSITION, not by world letter or world name. It never says 'Spiritual'. It reaches A->T only if the owner's letter order A,B,C,D is also the abstraction order, which it separately asserts at line 52: 'This World-order convention (high-abstraction at 1st, embodied at 4th) matches the Domain descent ordering in CAS (P > C > E > O).' That sentence is the ONLY place in the repo that links BOTH hypotheses to the same ordering - and it explicitly says the two axes 'do not collapse'.
Three separate scripts hardcode it with no version and no hash.

rows.why_this_row_is_CONTESTED: Both hypotheses are asserted in live repo artifacts, and CAS_FOUNDATIONAL_CLARIFICATIONS.md lines 308-310 makes them mutually exclusive as identities: 'The Domain axis ... specifies the ontological-substrate level ... The Register axis ... specifies the operational character. These are independent. A Principled-domain operation can occur in any of the four registers ... all four being ^2^P operations.' If Domain does not determine Register, then a single World letter cannot be identical to both. At most one of H-WD and H-WR is an identity; the other is at best a correlation. Nothing on disk decides which. No owner-authored artifact states either one.

axis_3_symbol_index_A1_D10_to_A0_D9.axis_status: EVIDENCED AS A CODE BIJECTION; MEANING-CONSISTENT ON 35 OF 40 ROWS (3 WEAK, 2 DIVERGENT)
axis_3_symbol_index_A1_D10_to_A0_D9.what_this_axis_is: This is registry known_conflict #1, element_indexing_A1_D10_vs_A0_D9 (P0_SEMANTIC_IDENTITY), whose required_resolution is: 'Publish and test a bijective code-and-meaning crosswalk; store both source_symbol and normalized_index in every artifact.' It is a TKS<->TKS index crosswalk, not a TKS<->CAS one, but the registry names it as the blocker on binding 6 and the pre-registration names it as the reason Arm C is unavailable (GATE2_ITEM4_PREREGISTRATION.md:155).
axis_3_symbol_index_A1_D10_to_A0_D9.THE_KEY_FINDING: The remap is NOT a shift by one and is NOT a rotation. Measured this session by reading both files: the zero-based canon puts IDEA at position 0 (B0 'Thought Form / A specific idea/concept', C0 'Emotional Concept / The idea of an emotion', D0 'Physical Template / Concept of a physical thing') and the owner's one-based scheme puts IDEA at position 10 ('Mental Idea', 'Emotional Idea', 'Physical Idea'). Every other position holds the SAME DIGIT in both schemes. So the crosswalk is IDENTITY on digits 1..9 and 10 <-> 0, with the world letter unchanged. That is exactly the same shape as the TKS-position -> CAS-Noetic map. The registry calls it 'a cyclic index remapping'; the measured structure is narrower and better-behaved than that phrase suggests, because 39 of the 40 codes are literally the same string.
axis_3_symbol_index_A1_D10_to_A0_D9.why_that_matters_for_future_agent_rule_2: future_agent_rule 2 forbids remapping A1-D10 to A0-D9 BY POSITION without a tested crosswalk. The map proposed here is not derived from position: it is derived from the NAMES on both sides, read from both files. A pure by-position remap (A1->A0, A2->A1, ... A10->A9) would put Mind at Idea's slot and is REFUTED by the name evidence. Stating that explicitly is the point of this section: the naive positional remap the rule warns against is not merely unratified, it is measurably wrong.
axis_3_symbol_index_A1_D10_to_A0_D9.caveat_that_is_not_smoothed_over: Code-bijectivity is trivial once the map is stated. MEANING-bijectivity is not established. The canon definitions are min 13 / mean 21.1 / max 36 chars of concrete gloss ('Woman, female person') against the owner's 71-686 char structural prose. Establishing that A5 in one scheme MEANS what A5 in the other means is a judgement I made by reading, not a test anyone ran. The registry asks for a 'tested' crosswalk. Nothing here is tested. This is a proposal for the owner to ratify, and ratifying it does not make it tested.
axis_3_symbol_index_A1_D10_to_A0_D9.does_this_unblock_arm_C: NO - and it must not be read that way. Even with this index crosswalk ratified, Arm C stays 'unavailable' on the 40-Element axis for an INDEPENDENT reason the pre-registration already froze at section 2.3: canon_elements_40.json's definition field is min 13 / mean 21.1 / max 36 chars against Arm A's mean 196.2, a ~9x length mismatch that violates spec 8.2's 'prompt style and length distribution' hold-constant. The pre-registration is LOCKED and says Arm C is unavailable. Nothing in this proposal changes that, and the run stays five-armed.

contested_summary.why_no_assistant_recommendation_on_the_a: I will state what the evidence weighs at, and then stop. Weighing on precedence alone, H_WR (World->Register) is ahead: its top source (CAS_FOUNDATIONAL_CLARIFICATIONS.md:346) sits at repository-normative tier 5, and the Gate 2 item 4 holdout bank - the one this experiment actually scores on - asserts Register and carries no CAS-domain field at all. Weighing on consequences, H_WD is ahead: it is already load-bearing in the 8,320-row label set behind the 95.625% GPT-NeoX-20B claim, so ratifying H_WR as an exclusive identity would put that label set on a different footing. Those two considerations point opposite ways, no owner-authored artifact decides between them, and the owner holds the prior under test in this experiment. An assistant recommendation here would be an assistant deciding the semantics of the owner's own ontology on a coin-flip, which is the failure mode the registry's future_agent_rules exist to stop.
contested_summary.narrower_decision_that_actually_unblocks: Gate 2 item 4 does not need the World axis SETTLED. It needs Arm D's second factor NAMED and HASHED before capture. The already-built Arm D payload (docs/working/gate2_closure/item4_arms/arm_D_compact_cas.json) emits both variants - D_REG_V1 (second factor = Register) and D_DOM_LITERAL_V1 (second factor = Domain) - so the owner can bind one for this run WITHOUT declaring an identity, and the registry's 'two separate versioned hypotheses' resolution stays intact for later. That is the minimum decision.

questions.question: Which axis is the SECOND FACTOR of the 40 Elements - the CAS Domain (P/C/E/O), or the CAS Register (T/A/f/E)? Pick ONE for this run. This does not have to settle the ontology; it has to name what Arm D compiles against.
questions.evidence_strength: CONTESTED. Both readings are live in the repo and CAS_FOUNDATIONAL_CLARIFICATIONS.md:308-310 makes them mutually exclusive as identities.
questions.what_a_wrong_answer_costs: Nothing statistically - Arm D is comparator-only and E2 is stamped CONDITIONAL either way - but the run would be measuring a compiled arm the owner does not recognise as CAS.

questions.question: IF DOMAIN: ratify A/Spiritual->P, B/Mental->C, C/Emotional->E, D/Physical->O? IF REGISTER: ratify A/Spiritual->|T, B/Mental->|A, C/Emotional->|f, D/Physical->|E?
questions.answer_format: YES / NO / NO-WITH-CORRECTION (state the corrected rows)
questions.evidence_strength: The ORDERING within each hypothesis is better evidenced than the hypothesis itself. Both candidate orderings run high-abstraction to concrete in the letter order A,B,C,D, and docs/reference/tks_28_foundations_translation_key.md:52 says so explicitly. So if you answer Q2, the four rows in Q3 follow with much less doubt than Q2 itself carries.

questions.question: Ratify the symbol-index crosswalk A1..D10 <-> A0..D9 as: same world letter, digits 1..9 unchanged, and 10 <-> 0 (Idea)? Note the four rows I flagged as not clean: A0 (canon 'Divine Blueprint' is a weak match for ^0 Idea), D5 and D6 (canon reads them as literal persons, 'Woman'/'Man'), and D8/D9 (canon reads Above/Below SPATIALLY as 'Elevation'/'Foundation' while CAS reads them CAUSALLY as Cause/Effect - the A, B and C worlds all read causally, only D switches).
questions.note: Answering this does NOT unblock Arm C. Arm C stays 'unavailable' for an independent, already-frozen reason: canon definitions average 21.1 chars against Arm A's 196.2, a ~9x length mismatch that violates spec 8.2. The run stays five-armed either way.

questions.affects: which Arm D payload is captured
questions.question: Bind Arm D to variant D_REG_V1 (Noetic definition + verbatim Register definition, 100% byte-verbatim from CAS_FOUNDATIONAL_CLARIFICATIONS.md) or D_DOM_LITERAL_V1 (Noetic definition + an assistant-assembled one-sentence Domain gloss)? Both are already built in arm_D_compact_cas.json. The assistant's recorded recommendation there is D_REG_V1, because D_DOM_LITERAL_V1's four domain sentences differ from one another by exactly one word, which makes it close to a 10-class arm wearing 40 labels.
questions.why_it_must_be_answered_before_capture: Pre-registration section 2.4 and the payload's own variant_binding block: promoting a variant after any number exists is post-hoc selection, which section 9.3 forbids.

after_answering: 1. Record the answers in a signed receipt alongside OWNER_SEMANTIC_AUTHORITY_REGISTRY_SIGNED_20260724.json.
2. Emit the ratified crosswalk as its own JSON with only the ratified rows, compute its sha256 over LF bytes, and write that hash into required_run_bindings[6] tks_to_cas_crosswalk_sha256.
3. Append it to GATE2_ITEM4_PREREGISTRATION.md as a hashed amendment, DATED, before any forward pass.
4. If Q2 selected an axis, re-run compile_arm_D_compact_cas.py bound to that variant and rehash the Arm D payload.

what_this_artifact_does_not_settle: It does not test anything. The registry asks for a TESTED crosswalk (known_conflict #1 required_resolution). Ratification publishes; it does not test.

It does not resolve known_conflict tks_world_to_cas_domain_and_register_collision. Q2/Q3 bind a working choice for one run; the registry's own resolution asks for both hypotheses preserved and each tested as a distinct multi-head probe, which is a separate piece of work.

It does not touch the 28-Foundation / 7-Drive position mapping (registry known_conflict tks_foundation_vs_cas_drive_position_mapping, P1_SEMANTIC_AXIS). docs/reference/tks_28_foundations_translation_key.md:29-41 position-matches TKS Foundation n to CAS Drive Fn, and its own line 68 records the 28 entries as scaffolded placeholders with TKS-source fields PENDING. That axis is out of scope here because the pre-registration section 4.4 dropped the 28-Foundation axis as claim-bearing.
It does not lift any claim status. Nothing here licenses an empirical claim, and the pre-registration's section 12 list is unchanged.

It does not make Arm D claim-bearing. Arm D stays comparator-only at precedence tier 7, and every A-vs-D number stays stamped CONDITIONAL_ON_UNRATIFIED_CROSSWALK until a signed artifact is hashed into binding 6.

one_notational_defect_found_in_passing.what: The 8,320-row export spells the element as '^1|P', '^2|C', etc.
one_notational_defect_found_in_passing.why_it_is_a_defect: The '|' is the CAS Register operator (Clarification 8 notation: ^n|R). Here it carries a DOMAIN letter. The correct CAS spelling for a Noetic-in-a-Domain is '^1^P'. This is the World/Domain/Register collision leaking into notation. Recorded, not fixed - fixing a shipped 8,320-row label set is not a Gate 2 item 4 action.
